finding_verdicts.title: Development snapshots repeat distribution validation

evidence.observation: On a cache miss the builder runs build, generate:check and validate consecutively, then collects and renders the source again to obtain snapshot plugin bytes.
generate:check is generate.mjs --check; validate is validate.mjs with strict completeness by default. No command indirection supplies a separate check here.
Strict check validates source, collects it, builds expected files and compares generated outputs without publication.
Default validation rejects incomplete source and, for complete source, uses the same collect/render/compare functions. Its incomplete-source error ordering differs from strict generation.
The common comparison checks safe expected files, exact bytes and the complete managed path set, so retained strict validate still owns these checks.

The injected runner currently accepts arbitrary run commands; tests cover snapshot layout/reuse, local changes/deletion, failure cleanup and concurrent publication, but do not establish a single validation command or cross-command diagnostic equivalence.

Test definitions cover successful generation/validation, deterministic read-only check, tampering, unexpected/missing output, unsafe generated/source paths and partial packaging. Several failures are tested through only one entry point, not an explicit equivalence matrix.

finding_verdicts.independent_assessment: The repeated complete-source pass/fail validation is supported. The title's literal same-validation reading needs narrowing: generateRepository requires complete source before checking for packaging, whereas validateRepository first allows incomplete source inspection and then checks for generated artifacts. An incomplete source tree with generated files can therefore produce a different first diagnostic even though both reject it. No successful snapshot acceptance difference was identified on stable complete inputs.
finding_verdicts.current_execution_path: New digest -> build -> generate:check -> strict validate -> render snapshot Codex bytes -> pack with lifecycle scripts suppressed -> final source fingerprint -> staging rename. Existing matching snapshot returns before these commands.
finding_verdicts.existing_mechanisms: Source-derived snapshot IDs, an existing-snapshot shortcut, unique staging, final source-drift rejection, --ignore-scripts packing and concurrent-winner handling already exist. Reuse checks manifest identity and required artifact existence; this review does not describe it as a full artifact-byte revalidation cache.
finding_verdicts.reproducible_scenario: In a separately authorized isolated checkout, arrange a cache-miss digest and instrument runCommand. The source-defined command sequence contains both complete distribution gates. As a separate negative control, remove a skill while retaining generated outputs to expose the different leading diagnostics. Neither scenario was executed here.
finding_verdicts.replacement_minimal_recommendation: Remove only buildDevSnapshot's immediately preceding generate:check after focused equivalence tests demonstrate that retained default strict validate rejects all unsafe/incomplete/tampered inputs and accepts the same complete stable inputs. Do not claim identical error ordering; preserve or deliberately document any externally relied-on build diagnostic. Keep the public generate:check command and later rendering needed to write the snapshot.
preserved_guarantees: Strict completeness, unknown/unresolved host-token rejection, safe paths, exact generated bytes and unexpected-file rejection remain mandatory.
Keep source fingerprints, staging cleanup, atomic publication and isolated packaging; do not introduce cross-run validation caches or skip artifact construction.
Do not apply this local deduplication to separate CI purposes, user test freshness hooks, installation verification or runtime identity.
finding_verdicts.expected_qualitative_effect: One repeated npm startup and source/render/generated-tree comparison may be removed on cache misses only. Magnitude is unmeasured; cache hits already bypass both commands.
finding_verdicts.validation_and_measurement_plan: Extend the injected-runner tests with command-count assertions and paired success/tamper/missing-source/unexpected-file/unsafe-path rejection cases. Preserve source-drift, cleanup and concurrent publication controls. Later compare equal-input cache-miss timings separately from cache hits with fixed toolchain and executable/source digests.
finding_verdicts.rough_complexity: Small command-path change plus bounded failure-equivalence tests; no new cache or public API required.
dependencies: Explicit handling of any relied-on diagnostic differences
finding_verdicts.confidence: High for repeated stable-input work; no measured performance impact.

related.relationship: Same validation mechanism sampled as sound in P11. P11 has no duplicate finding; F1 concerns consecutive orchestration calls, not weakening generator guarantees.

finding_verdicts.title: Q36 and Q38 execute the same restart-enabled baseline scenario

evidence.observation: Q36 calls the no-model wrapper; Q38 separately invokes the harness with restartReviewer:true. Q38's complete/hash/replay/duplicate assertions use fields available in Q36's localSmoke result.
The wrapper always selects restartReviewer:true, exposes sourceReads and recovery, and owns cleanup in a finally block through its own testContext.
Both normal calls create fresh isolated workspaces and author/reviewer actors; the harness returns sourceReads and recovery. Reliability is an explicit different branch.
The baseline actually restarts the reviewer, replays the exact record request, compares contexts and computes duplicateVerdicts. These assertions must not become inherited metadata.

Native test context propagates signal/diagnostics and supports active checks; the scope owns reverse-order disposal and aggregates failures. Q36's wrapper-created testContext supplies after only, while Q38 currently supplies native t.
Packed tests verify package inventory, negative controls, actual extracted entrypoint, serving identity and distinct reliability/remediation scenarios; they are not equivalent duplicate baselines.
The test file and standalone native qualification CLI are separate gates.
Snapshot CI likewise retains distinct generated/lint/acceptance/CLI boundaries.

finding_verdicts.independent_assessment: Scenario-level duplication and reusable result fields are confirmed. Identical execution is too broad: Q38 uses the native test lifecycle, including cancellation, while Q36 uses a wrapper owner without that signal. Consolidating assertions onto Q36 exactly as written would remove the native-context baseline path. This is a small lifecycle qualification to the proposal, not evidence that two full successful baseline runs are inherently necessary.
finding_verdicts.current_execution_path: Q36 -> wrapper -> baseline harness plus report shaping and finally cleanup; Q38 -> baseline harness under native test context. Both choose restartReviewer:true and the default server entrypoint.
finding_verdicts.existing_mechanisms: The harness already centralizes scenario construction. Wrapper localSmoke already contains all Q38 assertion fields. Fixture scopes own transports/directories and cleanup; separate packed, reliability, retirement, remediation and alias variants test distinct boundaries.
finding_verdicts.reproducible_scenario: After separate authorization, instrument only Q36/Q38 and count baseline harness and actor launches, then inject wrong source hashes, missing continuations, broken replay and duplicate verdicts. Also cancel the combined baseline during connection to verify that ownership guarantees survive. No qualification was run here.
finding_verdicts.replacement_minimal_recommendation: Consolidate the baseline assertions within one test callback and one real baseline run, but preserve the native test signal/diagnostics at the harness boundary as well as wrapper finally cleanup and report-shape assertions. If Q36 remains the sole runner, carry that native context through its existing ownership boundary before removing Q38. Otherwise retain both until this is covered. Do not share live scenario state between tests. Retain the standalone CLI gate and all distinct variant/packed tests.
preserved_guarantees: Keep complete exact source/hash assertions and real restart/replay/zero-duplicate checks.
Keep independent author/reviewer actors, unique roots, cancellation, reverse cleanup and failure reporting.
Retain CLI exit/report semantics and the package/entrypoint/platform boundaries; no automatic CLI or matrix deletion.
finding_verdicts.expected_qualitative_effect: Potential removal of one full baseline fixture/actor lifecycle per test-file execution, without claiming savings or dropping cancellation assurance.
finding_verdicts.validation_and_measurement_plan: Assert all former Q36/Q38 fields against the same returned result; retain faults that independently fail each assertion and a cancellation/cleanup control. Measure selected-file fixture and actor-launch counts, wall-time distribution and cleanup on fixed OS/runtime inputs only after implementation authorization.
finding_verdicts.rough_complexity: Small test consolidation with explicit lifecycle forwarding/coverage; no global fixture or result cache.
dependencies: Preservation of native test cancellation and wrapper cleanup ownership
finding_verdicts.confidence: High for duplicated scenario work and available fields; performance effect unmeasured.

finding_verdicts.acceptance_scope: Benchmark-only. No harmful contention, current process peak, timeout cause or optimal limit is established.

evidence.observation: The existing runner caps file concurrency by requested capacity, detected capacity and eight, exposes lower limits/serial mode, discovers canonical roots only and uses process isolation where supported. It does not implement nested-process accounting.
Definitions cover the capacity ceiling, lower limits, serial mode, delimiter behavior, actual distinct sentinel processes and archive exclusion. V03 did not rerun them.
A qualification file can launch separate stdio author/reviewer actors.
The packed test adds npm pack, an extracted-package server and scenario actors inside its file process.
CI selects multiple heavy acceptance files together; matrix cells are distinct hosted jobs, not one shared local CPU pool.
Lower concurrency and serial diagnosis are already documented, so no new scheduler is needed to test the hypothesis.

finding_verdicts.independent_assessment: Nested process topology is confirmed, but topology alone does not show costly contention. Existing controls already support the proposed discriminating experiment. Do not recast the title as a defect in the eight-file policy or infer live peak by multiplying ceilings.
finding_verdicts.current_execution_path: Runner bounds test-file processes; file-local pack/server/actor activity remains additional workload. Existing fixtures isolate their state.
finding_verdicts.existing_mechanisms: Capacity-aware ceiling, explicit lower limit, serial mode, canonical discovery, process isolation and owned cleanup already exist.
finding_verdicts.reproducible_scenario: Only in an authorized isolated experiment, compare the actual CI acceptance file set at limits 1, 2, 4 and 8, using the same built executable and runner configuration.
finding_verdicts.replacement_minimal_recommendation: Use the existing concurrency flag for a bounded benchmark. Change only a relevant acceptance-step limit if observed resource/latency evidence warrants it; retain a lane testing deliberate concurrency. Add no scheduler, semaphore or global cache now.
preserved_guarantees: Do not serialize concurrency/locking/replay behavior that the tests intentionally exercise.
Keep isolated roots, process isolation, cancellation, actor teardown and all assertions.
Measure cleanup/failure behavior separately and do not use real global homes or warm installed state.
finding_verdicts.expected_qualitative_effect: Unknown. A lower limit may improve tail behavior or may simply slow the run.
finding_verdicts.validation_and_measurement_plan: Alternate repeated limits with fixed source/executable identity, platform/runtime and workload. Observe actual process-tree peak, memory, IO, wall-time, failures and cleanup; separate cold/warm runs and standalone-heavy-file controls. Do not adopt a default change without material evidence.
finding_verdicts.rough_complexity: Bounded benchmark first; a command-option change only if supported.
finding_verdicts.confidence: High for topology and existing controls; unknown material contention.

Stdio mode launches dist/main.js and reconnects for activation replay. Returned JSON reports transport/scenario/timings/profile but no serving build/contract identity. Reconnection is part of the measured scenario.

The existing identity mechanism validates package/runtime inventory and embedded stamp, returns verified/unavailable, and freezes identity at module load. It is not merely the requested source revision or package version.

finding_verdicts.independent_assessment: The result-format gap is supported. Existing runtime identity solves the underlying identification problem but is not collected by these benchmark outputs. No stale executable incident, invalid historical result or speed saving was established. An experiment with separately retained executable/source evidence can already be credible; this finding concerns self-attribution of the script-produced JSON, not a blanket rejection of external evidence bundles.
finding_verdicts.current_execution_path: Product review measures prebuilt direct imports. Retirement measures direct tool invocation or a prebuilt stdio server and deliberate reconnect. Current outputs do not bind those executions to a verified identity.
finding_verdicts.existing_mechanisms: Reuse runtimeIdentity/workflow_runtime_info and existing A/B/unavailable controls; keep existing benchmark IO/byte/audit/profiling instrumentation rather than adding a framework.
finding_verdicts.reproducible_scenario: In an authorized isolated fixture, compare two same-package-version builds, or current source with retained old dist. finding_verdicts.replacement_minimal_recommendation: Add a compact compatible provenance envelope using the existing loaded-runtime identity mechanism, recording status, build/contract digests, Node/platform and fixture/measurement boundaries. For stdio, observe the actual process and record identity across deliberate reconnects outside workload counters/timers. For direct imports, capture the matching runtime identity coherently with module loading, not by reading an intended stamp after the timed run. Keep source revision/dirty-input digest separate and mark unavailable or mismatched identity visibly. Do not auto-build or refresh anything.

Confirm provenance is excluded from all timing/profile counters, including reconnect identity reads, and preserve existing replay/response-budget tests.
